raw_response:
I've been doing this for 50 years on this same land in Quzhou. My back isn't what it used to be and it's just my wife and me now, so I don't overwork myself. I know this land — I know when it's thirsty, I know when the wheat is pushing and needs a drink, I know what the millet can handle.

My main system is wheat in autumn, then millet on that same ground after the June harvest. That's what my father did and what works here. I keep a separate piece — about 3.5 mu — in maize because it pays better at market and the buyers come to us.

For wheat, I get seeds from the county cooperative. Not the old landraces, but the improved variety they sell us — Jimai or similar. I've seen those give decent yields without too much fuss. I till with the rotary machine my neighbor rents out — I can't manage the deep plough anymore alone. I put fertilizer down before sowing and again at jointing. Three waterings from the well: before planting to settle the seed bed, once at tillering when it gets cold-dry, and once at heading. I spray twice — once for rust, once before harvest if there's aphids.

For millet, I use seed I saved from last year's good plants. Millet is tough. It doesn't need much from me. Two waterings are enough, one fertilizer application at sowing, and I rarely need pesticide — maybe once if there's midge pressure.

For the maize plot, I buy hybrid seeds — Xianyu 335 or whatever the village shop has. Maize needs more from me: three waterings, more nitrogen, two pesticide runs for borer and leaf disease.

I'm not trying to maximize. I'm trying to get through the year with a decent harvest that the two of us can manage without hiring too much help.
